title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 23.

questions.question: Who did David make king over Israel when he was old and full of days?
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon
questions.explanation: David made Solomon his son king over Israel as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:1.

questions.question: Whom did David gather together along with the princes of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The priests and the Levites
questions.explanation: David gathered all the princes of Israel along with the priests and the Levites according to 1 Chronicles 23:2.

questions.question: From what age were the Levites numbered according to 1 Chronicles 23?
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty years and upward
questions.explanation: The Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and upward, as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:3.

questions.question: How many Levites were assigned to set forward the work of the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-four thousand
questions.explanation: Twenty-four thousand Levites were to set forward the work of the house of the LORD as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 23:4.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23, how many Levites were officers and judges?
questions.correctAnswer: Six thousand
questions.explanation: Six thousand Levites were officers and judges as per 1 Chronicles 23:4.

questions.question: How many Levites were porters according to the division David made?
questions.correctAnswer: Four thousand
questions.explanation: Four thousand Levites were porters as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:5.

questions.question: How many Levites praised the LORD with instruments made by David?
questions.correctAnswer: Four thousand
questions.explanation: Four thousand Levites praised the LORD with instruments made by David as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:5.

questions.question: Into which three courses did David divide the Levites?
questions.correctAnswer: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari
questions.explanation: David divided the Levites into the courses of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:6.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Gershon as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 23?
questions.correctAnswer: Laadan and Shimei
questions.explanation: The sons of Gershon were Laadan and Shimei according to 1 Chronicles 23:7.

questions.question: How many sons did Laadan have, and who was the chief?
options: Three sons; Jehiel was the chief
Four sons; Jahath was the chief
Two sons; Zetham was the chief
Three sons; Shelomith was the chief
questions.correctAnswer: Three sons; Jehiel was the chief
questions.explanation: Laadan had three sons; Jehiel was the chief, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:8.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Shimei?
questions.correctAnswer: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran
questions.explanation: The sons of Shimei were Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:9.

questions.question: True or False: Jahath was the chief among the sons of Shimei.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jahath was the chief among the sons of Shimei according to 1 Chronicles 23:11.

questions.question: True or False: The number of Levites was counted man by man from the age of twenty years and upward in David's time.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and upward, not twenty, as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:3.

questions.question: True or False: David said the LORD God of Israel had given rest to His people so they might dwell in Jerusalem forever.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David stated that the LORD God of Israel had given rest to His people so they may dwell in Jerusalem forever, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:25.

questions.question: True or False: David divided the Levites into courses named after the sons of Aaron.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David divided the Levites among the sons of Levi, namely Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, not after the sons of Aaron, as stated in 1 Chronicles 23:6.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Amram mentioned in 1 Chronicles 23?
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and Moses
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23:13 states that the sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses, establishing their lineage among the Levites.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23, what special role was Aaron separated for?
options: To sanctify the most holy things and burn incense before the LORD
To lead the Levites in praise
questions.correctAnswer: To sanctify the most holy things and burn incense before the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains that Aaron was set apart to sanctify the most holy things, burn incense, minister to the LORD, and bless in His name forever.

questions.question: Who was the chief of the sons of Gershom according to the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Shebuel
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23:16 specifically names Shebuel as the chief of the sons of Gershom.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 23 describe the descendants of Eliezer?
options: Eliezer had many sons and daughters
Eliezer had no other sons but Rehabiah, whose sons were very many
Eliezer had four sons who led the Levites
Eliezer was the chief of the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Eliezer had no other sons but Rehabiah, whose sons were very many
questions.explanation: Verse 17 clarifies that Eliezer had no other sons besides Rehabiah, and Rehabiah's descendants were numerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the sons of Izhar?
questions.correctAnswer: Shelomith was the chief
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23:18 identifies Shelomith as the chief among the sons of Izhar.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 23:19 teach about the sons of Hebron?
options: They were Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam
questions.correctAnswer: They were Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam
questions.explanation: Verse 19 lists the sons of Hebron as Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam, showing their order and significance.

questions.question: According to verses 21-22, what happened when Eleazar died without sons?
options: His daughters were taken by their brethren, the sons of Kish
His estate was given to the Levites
The priesthood was passed to his brother
questions.correctAnswer: His daughters were taken by their brethren, the sons of Kish
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23:22 explains that Eleazar died without sons, and his daughters were taken by the sons of Kish, their brethren, indicating family responsibility and inheritance customs.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faithfulness and responsibility can be drawn from the way the Levites were organized in 1 Chronicles 23?
options: Faithfulness requires clear roles and order in service
Faithfulness is shown by individual independence
Responsibility is optional in spiritual service
Only priests are responsible for worship
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness requires clear roles and order in service
questions.explanation: The chapter shows detailed divisions and roles among Levites (verses 12-24), demonstrating that faithful service to God involves organized responsibility and cooperation.

questions.question: How does the passage in 1 Chronicles 23:13-14 teach us about humility in service to God?
options: Even leaders like Aaron and Moses had specific roles and submitted to God's plan
Humility is shown by refusing to serve
Serving God is optional for leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Even leaders like Aaron and Moses had specific roles and submitted to God's plan
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 indicate that Aaron and Moses were given distinct roles, showing humility in accepting God’s designated service, which teaches believers to humbly embrace their God-assigned duties.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 23:20, Jesiah was the second son of Uzziel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly states that the sons of Uzziel were Michah the first and Jesiah the second, confirming Jesiah's position.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish, but Eleazar had many sons to continue his line.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains that Eleazar died without sons but had daughters, so the sons of Kish took them, indicating Eleazar had no sons to continue his lineage.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 23:13-17 teach us about the importance of legacy and spiritual heritage?
options: Spiritual heritage is passed through appointed families and their descendants
Legacy is unimportant in spiritual matters
Only Moses' sons mattered in the Levite lineage
Leadership is always inherited by the eldest son
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual heritage is passed through appointed families and their descendants
questions.explanation: Verses 13-17 trace the sons and descendants of Amram and Moses, emphasizing the continuity of spiritual service through families, highlighting the importance of legacy.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 23:18-20 reveal about the organization of the Levites?
options: They were organized by family clans with appointed chiefs
They functioned as individuals without grouping
questions.correctAnswer: They were organized by family clans with appointed chiefs
questions.explanation: The passages name chiefs of different clans (Shelomith, Jeriah, Michah), showing a structured leadership within the tribe of Levi.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 23:21, Mahli and Mushi were the sons of Merari.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explicitly states that the sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi, confirming the family lineage.

questions.question: Based on 1 Chronicles 23:17, how should we understand the value of multiplication and growth within spiritual families?
options: Growth and multiplication are signs of blessing and responsibility
Numbers are irrelevant in spiritual service
Growth is only physical, not spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: Growth and multiplication are signs of blessing and responsibility
questions.explanation: Verse 17 shows that Rehabiah had many sons, indicating that growth within spiritual families is a blessing and important for continued service.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 23.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23, from what age were Levites numbered for their service in the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: 20 years old
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states the Levites were counted from the age of twenty years and upward to do the service of the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What reason does David give for the Levites no longer carrying the tabernacle or its vessels?
options: Because the temple was now built
Because the people had rest and dwelt in Jerusalem forever
Because the priests took over all duties
questions.correctAnswer: Because the people had rest and dwelt in Jerusalem forever
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states that the LORD God of Israel had given rest to his people so they could dwell in Jerusalem forever, leading to the Levites no longer carrying the tabernacle as per verse 26.

questions.question: What was the primary role of the Levites according to 1 Chronicles 23:28?
options: To carry the ark of the covenant
To wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD
To write the law and teach the people
questions.correctAnswer: To wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 28 specifies their office was to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD in various sacred functions.

questions.question: Which of these offerings were the Levites responsible to prepare and manage, as listed in verse 29?
options: Shewbread, fine flour for meat offering, unleavened cakes
questions.correctAnswer: Shewbread, fine flour for meat offering, unleavened cakes
questions.explanation: Verse 29 enumerates these specific offerings and preparations as part of the Levites’ duties for the house of God.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23:30, when were the Levites to stand and thank and praise the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Both morning and evening
questions.explanation: Verse 30 clearly states they were to stand every morning and likewise at evening to thank and praise the LORD.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 23:31, on which occasions were burnt sacrifices to be offered continually before the LORD?
options: Only on the day of atonement
On sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts
On the first day of every month
questions.correctAnswer: On sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts
questions.explanation: Verse 31 specifies these times as when burnt sacrifices were to be offered continually before the LORD according to the commanded order.

questions.question: What charge were the Levites to keep according to 1 Chronicles 23:32?
options: Charge of the tabernacle, holy place, and the sons of Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: Charge of the tabernacle, holy place, and the sons of Aaron
questions.explanation: Verse 32 details that the Levites were to keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, the holy place, and the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23:23, who were the sons of Mushi?
questions.correctAnswer: Mahli, Eder, Jeremoth
questions.explanation: Verse 23 explicitly names Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth as the three sons of Mushi.

questions.question: What was the significance of Aaron and his sons as described in 1 Chronicles 23:13?
options: They were to lead Israel in battle
Separated to sanctify the most holy things and burn incense forever
They were given the role of Levite musicians
They were tasked with carrying the ark
questions.correctAnswer: Separated to sanctify the most holy things and burn incense forever
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains Aaron was separated to sanctify the most holy things, burn incense, minister before the LORD, and bless in His name forever.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified in the way David organizes the Levites by their families and roles in 1 Chronicles 23?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter begins and ends with the roles and organization of the Levites (verses 1 and 32), creating an inclusio framing the Levites’ duties throughout, emphasizing their sacred service.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'praise' in 1 Chronicles 23:5 is related to which of the following meanings?
questions.correctAnswer: To sing with musical instruments
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root used here (הלל, halal) often means 'to praise' especially by singing or playing instruments, as indicated in verse 5 mentioning instruments made for praise.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of the Levites assisting the priests in sacred duties as described in 1 Chronicles 23?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 4:1-33
questions.explanation: Numbers 4 details the duties and responsibilities of the Levites in assisting the priests with the tabernacle service, directly paralleling 1 Chronicles 23.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the fulfillment of priestly service and intercession that echoes the role of Aaron and his sons in 1 Chronicles 23:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 7:23-28
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7 discusses Jesus as the eternal high priest, fulfilling and superseding the priestly roles of Aaron and his sons described in 1 Chronicles 23:13.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23:26, how did the role of the Levites change after the people of Israel had rest?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states the Levites would no longer carry the tabernacle or its vessels, indicating a change in their role after Israel's rest in Jerusalem.

questions.question: The enumeration of the Levites from twenty years old and upward in 1 Chronicles 23 contradicts the earlier age of thirty years given in verse 3 for their numbering.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 3 mentions numbering Levites from thirty years old, but later, in verses 24 and 27, this age is lowered to twenty years old, reflecting a change in requirement, not contradiction.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about the priesthood is taught in 1 Chronicles 23:13 regarding Aaron and his sons?
options: Aaron and his sons are consecrated forever to sanctify the most holy things and minister before the LORD
Aaron and his sons serve temporarily until a new priesthood is established
Aaron and his sons were only responsible for teaching the law to Israel
Aaron and his sons were kings alongside Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons are consecrated forever to sanctify the most holy things and minister before the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23:13 states that Aaron was separated to sanctify the most holy things together with his sons forever to minister unto the LORD and bless in His name, teaching the doctrine of a perpetual priesthood. This reveals the doctrine of the enduring, God-ordained priesthood, which foreshadows Christ as our eternal High Priest (Hebrews 7:23-24).

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 23:4-5, how does the division of Levites into different groups illustrate the doctrine of service in God's house?
options: The Levites were divided into workers, officers, porters, and musicians to fulfill distinct roles in worship and governance
All Levites performed the same tasks interchangeably without distinction
Levites were assigned only to musical praise with no administrative duties
Levites were responsible only for carrying the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites were divided into workers, officers, porters, and musicians to fulfill distinct roles in worship and governance
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 explain the Levites were assigned specific roles: 24,000 for the work of the house, 6,000 as officers and judges, 4,000 porters, and 4,000 who praised the LORD with instruments. This division teaches the doctrine of ordered worship and the necessity of diverse ministries within the church body (1 Corinthians 12:12-27).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in 1 Chronicles 23:25 when David acknowledges that the LORD has given rest to His people?
options: God's providence in establishing peace and stability for His covenant people
God's temporary indifference to Israel's affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence in establishing peace and stability for His covenant people
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23:25 says that the LORD God of Israel hath given rest unto His people to dwell in Jerusalem forever. This reveals God's providential care and faithfulness to His covenant promises, demonstrating His attribute of sovereign providence (Psalm 4:8).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 23:26-27 teach about the sanctification of the Levites’ service in the temple?
options: The Levites are sanctified by no longer carrying the tabernacle but serving from age twenty and upward
Levites continue to carry the tabernacle indefinitely
Levites serve only in military roles
Levites are relieved from all temple duties
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites are sanctified by no longer carrying the tabernacle but serving from age twenty and upward
questions.explanation: Verses 26-27 state that Levites shall no longer carry the tabernacle nor its vessels but are numbered from twenty years old and above for service. This shows the sanctification of their role is defined by God’s order, marking a transition to a settled worship system (Numbers 8:24-25).

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 23:28 teach about the Levites' role in the purification and service of the house of God?
options: Levites wait on the sons of Aaron in courts, chambers, purification, and service of the house
Levites have no role in purification rituals
Levites serve only as guards outside the temple
Levites are responsible for teaching only, not service
questions.correctAnswer: Levites wait on the sons of Aaron in courts, chambers, purification, and service of the house
questions.explanation: Verse 28 clarifies the Levites’ office was to wait on Aaron’s descendants for the service of the LORD, including purifying holy things and ministering in various temple areas, teaching the doctrine of sanctification and holy service (Hebrews 9:13-14).

questions.question: From 1 Chronicles 23:30-31, what does the continual morning and evening praise teach about the nature of worship?
options: Worship should be continual and ordered according to God's command, reflecting thankfulness and reverence
Worship should be silent without song
Worship is only for special occasions
questions.correctAnswer: Worship should be continual and ordered according to God's command, reflecting thankfulness and reverence
questions.explanation: Verses 30-31 show that Levites stood every morning and evening to thank and praise the LORD and offered sacrifices continually on sabbaths, new moons, and feasts. This teaches the doctrine of regulated, continual worship in reverence and gratitude (Psalm 92:1-2).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 23:24-25 together reveal a theological transition in Israel’s worship life?
options: Levites begin service from twenty years old due to established rest and permanent dwelling in Jerusalem
Levites continue nomadic service carrying the tabernacle
Levites stop all service in the house of the LORD
Levites are replaced by foreign priests
questions.correctAnswer: Levites begin service from twenty years old due to established rest and permanent dwelling in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 24 numbers Levites from twenty years old upward for service, then verse 25 explains that because the LORD has given rest so Israel may dwell in Jerusalem forever, the nature of Levite service adapts. This shows the shift from a mobile tabernacle to a permanent temple worship system (Deuteronomy 12:10).

questions.question: What does the genealogical detail in 1 Chronicles 23:12-21 reveal about God’s providential ordering of priestly and Levitical service?
options: God providentially ordains distinct family lines within Levi for specific temple duties
All Levites serve identically without distinction
Genealogy is irrelevant to temple service
Only Moses' descendants serve in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially ordains distinct family lines within Levi for specific temple duties
questions.explanation: Verses 12-21 detail the sons of Kohath, Gershon, and Merari and their descendants, showing God’s providence in appointing specific families for various temple roles, affirming divine order and holiness in worship (Exodus 28:1-3).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the detailed numbering and division of Levites in 1 Chronicles 23 is merely bureaucratic and lacks theological significance. What does 1 Chronicles 23:1-6 and 23:28-32 actually teach about the spiritual and redemptive function of this organization?
options: The division reflects God's ordained order for sanctified worship and ongoing mediation before the LORD
The division is a political maneuver with no spiritual basis
Levites were numbered only for military reasons
The division is symbolic but not meant to be implemented
questions.correctAnswer: The division reflects God's ordained order for sanctified worship and ongoing mediation before the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 1-6 describe David’s establishment of Solomon’s kingship and the structured organization of Levites, while verses 28-32 emphasize their role in ministering, purifying, and serving continually in the house of the LORD. This shows the theological truth that worship requires divine order and mediation, countering scepticism (Hebrews 8:6).

questions.question: What doctrine about the permanence of God's covenant people is suggested by David making Solomon king in 1 Chronicles 23:1?
options: God’s covenant promises include an enduring dynasty and leadership over Israel
Kingship is temporary and irrelevant to God’s plan
David was the last king chosen by God
Solomon’s reign was accidental and not divinely ordained
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant promises include an enduring dynasty and leadership over Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows David, old and full of days, making Solomon king, reaffirming God’s covenant with David for an everlasting dynasty (2 Samuel 7:16) and the fulfillment of God’s sovereign plan for Israel’s leadership.

questions.question: How do 1 Chronicles 23:7-11 illustrate the doctrine of family responsibility and inheritance within Levitical service?
options: The sons of Laadan and Shimei are detailed with chiefs named, showing family heads’ roles and combined reckoning when few sons exist
Family divisions are abolished for Levites
Only eldest sons serve with no regard for other children
Family names are irrelevant to temple duties
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Laadan and Shimei are detailed with chiefs named, showing family heads’ roles and combined reckoning when few sons exist
questions.explanation: Verses 7-11 provide genealogical detail about Laadan and Shimei’s sons, highlighting the importance of family leadership and inheritance in organizing temple service, which reflects God-ordained familial order (Exodus 28:1).

questions.question: What theological significance does the statement in 1 Chronicles 23:14 about Moses’ sons being named of the tribe of Levi hold?
options: It affirms the continuation of priestly and Levitical lines through Moses’ descendants
Moses’ sons were excluded from Levitical service
Moses’ sons had no role in Israel’s worship
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the continuation of priestly and Levitical lines through Moses’ descendants
questions.explanation: Verse 14 identifies Moses’ sons as from the tribe of Levi, underscoring the continuation of God’s appointed priestly lineage through Moses, emphasizing God’s faithfulness in sustaining worship and covenant service (Exodus 6:20).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God’s holiness and order is conveyed by comparing 1 Chronicles 23:13 and 23:32 regarding the responsibilities of Aaron’s sons and the Levites?
options: Aaron’s sons are set apart to sanctify and bless, while Levites assist in service and guard the holy place, together maintaining God’s holiness
Aaron’s sons and Levites have interchangeable roles with no distinction
Both groups serve only in musical praise
Levites perform all duties including sacrifices without priestly mediation
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron’s sons are set apart to sanctify and bless, while Levites assist in service and guard the holy place, together maintaining God’s holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains Aaron and his sons’ unique sanctifying role, while verse 32 assigns Levites the charge of the tabernacle, holy place, and service alongside Aaron’s sons. This distinction affirms the doctrine of God’s holiness requiring ordered mediation and service (Leviticus 10:10-11).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 23:22 demonstrate God’s providence and justice in caring for daughters when a Levite dies without sons?
options: Daughters inherit and are cared for by their brethren, showing God’s provision for justice and family protection
Daughters are excluded and left destitute
Only sons inherit with no care for daughters
Levites do not have family inheritance laws
questions.correctAnswer: Daughters inherit and are cared for by their brethren, showing God’s provision for justice and family protection
questions.explanation: Verse 22 says Eleazar died without sons but had daughters, who were taken by their brethren, illustrating God’s justice and providential care for family continuity and protection of women in inheritance (Numbers 27:1-11).

questions.question: What narrative arc connecting the Levitical service in 1 Chronicles 23 to the broader redemptive story is shown in verses 13 and 14?
options: The priestly roles of Aaron’s descendants and Moses’ sons prefigure the ultimate High Priest, Jesus Christ, who mediates perfectly before God
Levitical service is unrelated to redemption
Only Moses is the mediator, no priesthood continuation
questions.correctAnswer: The priestly roles of Aaron’s descendants and Moses’ sons prefigure the ultimate High Priest, Jesus Christ, who mediates perfectly before God
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 describe the separation of Aaron and his sons for eternal priestly service and the inclusion of Moses’ sons, pointing forward typologically to Christ as the eternal High Priest who fulfills and perfects this mediation (Hebrews 7:23-28).
